findings.summary: Three drafts eliminate the sampled second decoder row tile, but improve evaluator p50 by only 1.0% while worsening p95 and throughput. Retain four drafts.
observations: NACA ordinary-call median is 2.242 s; rendering + OCR accounts for 93.5% of mean wall time and embedding 5.6%. Instrumented frozen outputs passed.

Across four bounded 32-iteration captures, narrow output/down projections used one row tile in 102 iterations and two in none. The prior four-draft profile used two in 99 iterations. These are launch-grid counts, not full-call time shares.
NACA accepts 3.1% of proposed tokens, averaging 1.093 output tokens per speculative step in the ordinary diagnostic calls.
GPU busy averages 68–82% across only seven one-second samples per device. This measures kernel activity, not percentage of peak compute or bandwidth.
The full evaluator passed 60 paired calls and 5,580 raw EOS completions. Three drafts gain 1.0% p 50 speedup but lose 2.9% p 95 speedup and 1.2% throughput versus the fresh four-draft control.
findings.next_step: Keep four drafts and test six concurrent requests per GPU. Six × five verification rows fits30 rows, potentially avoiding a second 32-row tile without losing the fourth speculative position.
findings.optimization: Compare server concurrency six against a fresh eight-request control with four drafts, fixed 32 tiles, worker rendering and four-GPU embeddings. Verify actual grids and all frozen outputs.
